exam.tagline: The NCCA-accredited credential for non-commercial foodservice managers — the CDM, CFPP is the federally referenced standard for directing healthcare and institutional foodservice.
exam.description: The Certified Dietary Manager, Certified Food Protection Professional (CDM, CFPP) is the nationally recognized credential for professionals who manage foodservice operations and lead nutrition care in non-commercial settings such as hospitals, long-term care, schools, and correctional facilities. It is awarded by the Certifying Board for Dietary Managers (CBDM) on behalf of the Association of Nutrition & Foodservice Professionals (ANFP) and is NCCA-accredited. Federal regulations for skilled nursing facilities (42 CFR §483.60) effectively require a CDM, CFPP or equivalent qualified dietary professional to direct foodservice, making the credential a strong employment driver. Candidates qualify through education-and-experience pathways and pass a 160-question exam; the credential sits at the top of the dietary/foodservice management ladder alongside registered dietitians.

quickAnswer.summary: The CDM, CFPP is the NCCA-accredited dietary management credential, earned by passing a 160-question (140 scored), 3-hour computer-based exam delivered by PSI, with a criterion-referenced passing standard.
advantages: NCCA-accredited and the nationally recognized standard for non-commercial foodservice management
Effectively required by federal SNF regulation (42 CFR §483.60) to direct healthcare foodservice
Validates both food protection (sanitation/safety) and dietary management (nutrition, personnel, business) competence
Portable across healthcare, long-term care, schools, and correctional foodservice
Strong employment security with roughly 72–75% first-time pass rates and a clear renewal path

roadmap: Confirm your eligibility pathway (ANFP program, degree, course + experience, or military)
Submit the online application with fees and documentation to CBDM
Schedule your 90-day window exam with PSI (test center or remote proctoring)
Activate your credential within one year of passing
Recertify annually (fee) and every 3 years (45 CE hours)
exam.prerequisites: A combination of formal education (accredited post-secondary) and full-time non-commercial foodservice management experience via one of CBDM's eligibility pathways; there is no single standalone course prerequisite.
exam.eligibility: CDM, CFPP eligibility runs through several CBDM pathways that each pair accredited education with full-time non-commercial (institutional) foodservice management experience — the more education you have, the less experience required. Pathway I: graduate of an ANFP-approved foodservice manager training program (120 hours didactic + 150 hours field experience). Pathway II: a 2-year, 4-year, or higher college degree in foodservice management, nutrition, culinary arts, hotel-restaurant management, or a related field. Pathway III(a): completion of a 90-hour foodservice course plus 2 years of full-time non-commercial foodservice management experience. Pathway III(b): completion of the classroom portion of an approved program plus 2 years of qualifying experience. Pathway IV: approved military dietary manager training. Pathway V: a college degree in another field plus 5 years of full-time non-commercial foodservice management experience. Commercial restaurant experience generally does not count.

examMeta.pass: Criterion-referenced cut score set by modified Angoff; historically ~70% of scored items (about 98 of 140). Reported pass/fail with domain feedback.
examMeta.fee: $425 exam/application fee (2026). ANFP membership and credential activation are handled separately.
examMeta.format: Computer-based, single-best-answer multiple choice delivered by PSI at 300+ test centers or approved remote online proctoring
examMeta.admin: Certifying Board for Dietary Managers (CBDM) on behalf of ANFP

topics.name: Foodservice

topics.name: Nutrition
topics.note: Nutrition screening, diet orders, therapeutic/texture-modified diets, Nutrition Care Process, education.

topics.name: Personnel and Communications

topics.note: Budgeting, food cost, purchasing specs/bids, cost control, department layout, records.

costBreakdown.total: $425 exam fee (2026); ANFP membership/activation billed separately
costBreakdown.footnote: The $425 is the exam application fee as of 2026; ANFP membership dues and credential activation are handled separately and may be bundled. Fees and policies can change — confirm on cbdmonline.org before applying. A new application and fee are required for each retake.

exam.audience: Dietary managers, foodservice directors, and aspiring managers in healthcare, long-term care, schools, and correctional foodservice who direct non-commercial food operations.
exam.time: Several weeks to months of prep; exam itself 3 hours

faqs.q: What are the CDM, CFPP eligibility pathways?
faqs.a: CBDM offers several pathways pairing accredited education with full-time non-commercial foodservice management experience. Pathway I is an ANFP-approved training program (120 hrs didactic + 150 hrs field); Pathway II is a foodservice/nutrition/culinary degree; Pathways III(a)/(b) combine a 90-hour course or approved classroom with 2 years of experience; Pathway IV is military dietary manager training; Pathway V is a non-related degree plus 5 years of experience. Commercial restaurant experience generally does not qualify.

faqs.q: How much does the exam cost?
faqs.a: The CDM, CFPP exam application fee is $425 as of 2026. ANFP membership and credential activation are billed separately and may be offered as a bundle. You must pay a new application fee each time you retake.

The exam is criterion-referenced: CBDM sets a cut score using a modified-Angoff procedure with practicing CDM, CFPPs. Historically about 70% of the 140 scored items (roughly 98 questions) has been required, and results are reported as pass/fail with domain-level feedback rather than a numeric percentage. First-time pass rates are about 72–75%.

faqs.q: How do I maintain the CDM, CFPP?
faqs.a: You pay an annual certification fee and, every three years, complete and report at least 45 continuing education hours — including at least 9 in Sanitation and Safety and at least 1 in Professional Ethics. You must also activate your credential within one year of passing the exam, or it is terminated.

You must wait 90 days before reapplying, and there is no limit on retake attempts. Each retake requires a new exam application and fee. Use your domain feedback report to focus study on your weakest areas.

summaryPoints: CDM, CFPP is the NCCA-accredited dietary management credential, earned via a 160-question, 3-hour PSI-delivered exam (2026 fee $425).
Five blueprint domains (2025): Sanitation & Safety 24%, Foodservice 22%, Nutrition 20%, Personnel & Communications 20%, Business Operations 14%.
Eligibility combines accredited education with non-commercial foodservice management experience across six pathways.
Renew annually (fee) and every 3 years with 45 CE hours (≥9 sanitation/safety, ≥1 ethics); federally referenced for SNF foodservice direction.

program.about: The Association of Nutrition & Foodservice Professionals (ANFP) is the national membership association for food and nutrition professionals in non-commercial foodservice. Its certifying arm, the Certifying Board for Dietary Managers (CBDM), develops and administers the NCCA-accredited CDM, CFPP credential and is referenced in federal regulations (42 CFR §483.60) for directing skilled-nursing foodservice.

registrationSteps.title: Review eligibility pathways
registrationSteps.description: Choose the CBDM pathway that fits your education and non-commercial foodservice management experience (ANFP program, degree, 90-hour course + experience, military, or other degree + experience).

registrationSteps.title: Submit the online application
registrationSteps.description: Apply through cbdmonline.org with the $425 exam fee and verifiable documentation (transcripts, training proof, experience verification). If requirements aren't met within 90 days, the application is voided.
registrationSteps.note: You must attest you have read the Candidate Handbook.

registrationSteps.title: Await eligibility approval
registrationSteps.description: CBDM emails your eligibility status. About 7–14 days after approval, PSI emails scheduling instructions.

registrationSteps.title: Schedule with PSI
registrationSteps.description: Book your exam at one of 300+ PSI test centers or via approved remote online proctoring. You must test within your 90-day window or the application and fees are forfeited.

registrationSteps.title: Take and pass the exam
registrationSteps.description: Bring two forms of ID and complete the 160-question, 3-hour exam. Results are reported pass/fail with domain feedback.

registrationSteps.title: Activate and maintain
registrationSteps.description: Activate your credential within one year of passing, pay the annual certification fee, and complete 45 CE hours every 3 years (≥9 sanitation/safety, ≥1 ethics).

program.proctoring: Computer-based, single-best-answer multiple choice delivered by PSI at 300+ U.S. test centers or via approved remote online proctoring. You answer one question per page, may flag and review, and the clock runs during breaks.
program.retakePolicy: If you do not pass, you must wait 90 days before reapplying, with no limit on attempts. Each retake requires a new exam application and the full fee. Candidates typically use their domain feedback to target weak areas before retesting.
program.recertification: Maintain active status by paying the annual certification fee. Every three years, complete and self-report at least 45 continuing-education hours, including a minimum of 9 in Sanitation and Safety and 1 in Professional Ethics. CE must be earned and reported only after the credential is activated; failure to meet requirements can trigger a CE audit and credential termination.
program.scoreReporting: Results are reported as pass/fail with diagnostic feedback by domain rather than a single public percentage. CBDM sets the cut score using a modified-Angoff procedure; historically about 70% of the 140 scored items is required.
program.refundPolicy: The exam fee is paid with the application; if eligibility requirements are not met within 90 days the application is voided (fees forfeited). You must schedule and complete the exam within the 90-day testing window or the application and fees are forfeited. Confirm current refund/reschedule rules in the Candidate Handbook.
program.providersNote: The CDM, CFPP exam is administered by CBDM through its testing partner PSI, which operates 300+ test centers and provides remote online proctoring.

orgFaqs.q: How do I apply for the CDM, CFPP exam?
orgFaqs.a: Apply online at cbdmonline.org, choose your eligibility pathway, upload documentation, and pay the $425 fee. After CBDM approval, PSI emails scheduling instructions; you must test within 90 days.

orgFaqs.q: How do I maintain my CDM, CFPP?
orgFaqs.a: Pay the annual certification fee and, every three years, report 45 CE hours (≥9 sanitation/safety, ≥1 ethics). Activate within one year of passing or the credential is terminated.

orgFaqs.q: Why is the CDM, CFPP important for employers?
orgFaqs.a: Federal SNF regulation (42 CFR §483.60) effectively requires a CDM, CFPP or equivalent to direct foodservice, so many healthcare and long-term-care employers specifically seek or require the credential.
